name: Singapore
tagline: Everything in English — and a subsidy that comes with a three-year contract
summary: Singapore runs entirely in English and reads the IB directly. The headline price is not the price: international students can take the MOE Tuition Grant, which brings tuition at NUS and NTU down to about SGD 21,400–22,200 a year, in exchange for a contract, guaranteed by two sureties, to work for a Singapore entity for three years after graduating. You choose it by ticking a box on the application form. NUS closes 17 February 2027 and NTU 19 March 2027; LASALLE's arts window closes as early as 1 November 2026.
whyConsider: Every degree is taught in English, and NUS and NTU are large research universities with international reputations.
The MOE Tuition Grant cuts international tuition from roughly SGD 33,400–40,600 a year to roughly SGD 21,400–22,200 at NUS and NTU — if you accept the service obligation.

The IB is read directly: NUS treats the IB Diploma as its own applicant group with its own window, and SMU does not ask IB Diploma holders for SAT, IELTS or TOEFL — though its Law and Computing & Law degrees want English A at grade 6 or 7 (HL or SL), with shortfalls considered case by case.
The three-year service obligation is, viewed differently, a guaranteed graduate-employment pathway into Singapore's job market — and Singapore actively wants the people it has subsidised to stay.
SUTD, built with MIT, runs a genuinely unusual design-led engineering curriculum with no departments in the first year.

The MOE Tuition Grant cuts NTU's international fee from roughly SGD 36,350–40,600 a year to roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 — about SGD 60,000–75,000 across a four-year degree — if you accept the service obligation.

Singapore has thought about the July problem and says what it does. NTU takes your application on predicted grades in March and wants the real results within three days of release; NUS tells May-session IB candidates they will hear by the third week of July.
The three-year service obligation, read the other way round, is a guaranteed graduate pathway into Singapore's job market — and Singapore actively wants the people it has subsidised to stay.
Offers are accepted once, through a shared Joint Acceptance Portal across the six Autonomous Universities, rather than replied to one by one.
SUTD, built with MIT, runs a genuinely unusual design-led curriculum with a common first year and no departments.
watchOuts: The Tuition Grant service obligation is a contract and it should be read as one. NTU states that a non-Singaporean who takes the grant signs an agreement that contractually obliges them to work in a Singapore entity for three years after graduating. MOE adds that only full-time employment after graduation counts, that a job search in Singapore typically takes about six months, and that deferring the bond for postgraduate study needs approval at least eight weeks in advance. Taking the grant is a decision about where you live into the 2030s.

You do not sign it alone. The agreement requires two sureties of any nationality, over 21 and under 65, not undischarged bankrupts, with the financial means to cover the liability — MOE encourages immediate family. You and your sureties are jointly liable for liquidated damages if the bond is not served.

The exposure is not only at the end. MOE states that a student who withdraws from the course midway is liable, with their sureties, for liquidated damages on the Tuition Grant received plus 10% compounded interest a year, with late-payment interest on top. Illness, homesickness or a change of mind in second year all fall inside that.

You elect the grant on the application form, months before anyone explains it, and sign the agreement in September or October once you are already in Singapore. By then you have flown, paid and moved in. Treat the tick-box as the decision point.

The deadlines are not shared and are not close together. LASALLE asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, NUS closes 17 February 2027, NTU closes 19 March 2027, and SUTD, SIT, SMU, SUSS and NAFA have not yet published 2027 dates (SMU's and SIT's 2026 cycles closed on 19 March 2026). There is no single date to remember and no portal that will remember it for you.

NTU will not consider a May-session IB candidate for Medicine, the Renaissance Engineering Programme, or Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education), because those decide before your results exist. That is a whole category of ambition closed off by a calendar.

Actual IB results are due at NTU within three days of release — the first week of July, in the middle of the Danish summer holiday. Both NTU and NUS make it mandatory to authorise the IB to release your transcript to them (NUS institute code 000690); ask your IB coordinator before July.
SUSS opens applications for its July 2027 intake in November 2026. James Cook University Singapore's 2027 dates are not given here: check its admissions page.
Tuition is given here for NTU (2026 entrants) and NUS (AY2026/2027 entrants) only. Do not assume NUS's or NTU's numbers apply to SMU or SUTD.

Whether an international student at LASALLE or NAFA can take the Tuition Grant, and would therefore be bonded, is not established. The University of the Arts Singapore names only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents and refers the question back to the two colleges. Ask before you assume either way.
Yale-NUS College has closed — it took its final cohort in 2021 and no longer admits students. NUS College is the successor honours college, and it is a different thing.
Indicative grade profiles are published for the Singapore-Cambridge A-level, not usually for the IB. Ask admissions directly for the IB equivalent rather than trusting a figure from a forum.
Singapore is expensive to live in, off campus in particular. Campus accommodation is the realistic option and is not guaranteed for all years.

If you can claim Danish SU, it works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk early. If you cannot claim it, check whether your own country's student finance covers a degree outside Europe.

feeContext.summary: Singapore does not recognise EU or EEA status. Its categories are Singapore Citizen, Singapore Permanent Resident and International Student, and an EU/EEA student is the third. See the non-EU row.

At NTU, for a student accepted in 2026 and with the rate fixed at the year-of-entry level for the whole degree: roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 a year with the MOE Tuition Grant, and SGD 36,350 (non-laboratory) to SGD 40,600 (laboratory-based) without it, inclusive of 9% GST. Medicine is non-subsidised only at SGD 91,250 a year for non-ASEAN internationals, and the Renaissance Engineering Programme non-subsidised at SGD 32,000. NUS, for AY2026/2027 entrants: SGD 21,400 a year with the grant in most faculties (SGD 22,200 business, SGD 30,450 law) and SGD 33,400–39,700 without it. SMU and SUTD figures are not given here, and these do not apply to them.

sectorLandscape.summary: Singapore's post-secondary system divides three ways, and the division decides the calendar, the money and the degree. Six Autonomous Universities — NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS, named as a group by the universities themselves — are publicly funded, carry the MOE Tuition Grant and settle their offers through one shared Joint Acceptance Portal. The two arts institutions, LASALLE and NAFA, now award their degrees through the University of the Arts Singapore and admit on portfolio and audition months earlier. Everything else is a registered Private Education Institution, including the Australian, American and French branch campuses, which award the parent's degree on a trimester calendar. Below all of this sits a route rarely mentioned to foreigners: the five polytechnics and the Institute of Technical Education, which are where most Singaporeans actually go.

routes.what: NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS. Government-funded, degree-awarding in their own right, and the only institutions where the MOE Tuition Grant and its three-year service obligation apply to an international student. You apply to each separately — six forms, six fees, six deadlines from November to March — and then accept one offer through a single Joint Acceptance Portal that lists all of them.
routes.note: The group is not a ranking. SIT is an applied university whose intake is overwhelmingly domestic polytechnic graduates, SUSS is built around part-time and flexible study, and SUTD is tiny and design-led. Only NUS, NTU and SMU are what a European would picture.

routes.what: LASALLE College of the Arts and the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, allied since 2024 into the University of the Arts Singapore, which now validates, confers and awards their degrees — LASALLE's were previously awarded by Goldsmiths, University of London. Entry is on portfolio and audition, with one intake each August and a deadline that falls the previous November, months ahead of the universities.
routes.note: Whether an international student here can take the MOE Tuition Grant is not established. UAS names Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents as eligible and says nothing about anyone else.

routes.englishName: private institution or foreign branch campus
routes.what: Registered private providers, including the branch campuses — James Cook University Singapore, Curtin Singapore, DigiPen Singapore, ESSEC Asia-Pacific — and SIM Global Education, which delivers partner universities' degrees without awarding its own. The degree is Australian, American, British or French rather than Singaporean, the structure is usually trimesters with several intakes a year, and the MOE Tuition Grant does not reach here.
routes.note: Singapore registers these institutions for a fixed term rather than chartering them, and the registration number and expiry date are published on their own pages. A registration expiring inside the length of your degree is a fair question to ask.

routes.what: Five polytechnics — Singapore, Ngee Ann, Temasek, Nanyang and Republic — awarding three-year applied diplomas that are the ordinary post-secondary destination for a large share of Singaporeans, and a recognised route onward into the Autonomous Universities with advanced standing. This is Singapore's answer to the Danish erhvervsakademi and it is rarely described to a foreign applicant.
routes.note: Not covered here. Whether an IB Diploma holder from abroad can enrol, what it costs and whether the Tuition Grant applies are all open questions. The route is large, and it explains why SIT's admissions calendar is built around polytechnic results rather than IB ones.

routes.what: The ITE, awarding Nitec and Higher Nitec vocational qualifications below diploma level, feeding into the polytechnics and into work. It appears on this page because LASALLE's Early Admission Exercise names final-year Nitec and Higher Nitec students alongside IB Year 4 students, which is the kind of detail that shows where the system's ladders actually are.

notes: Grouping decision. institutionGrouping is "jurisdiction" with three jurisdictions each of kind "sector". The division is not a convenience: whether an institution is an Autonomous University decides whether the MOE Tuition Grant and its three-year bond exist for you at all, whether you accept through the Joint Acceptance Portal, and whether your deadline falls in March or the previous November. Grouping by city would have been meaningless in a country that is one city. The "sector" grouping was considered and rejected because it carries no Application Route, and each of these three divisions has a different one.
The single most urgent item in this record is LASALLE: its window for August 2027 opens on 1 October 2026 and closes on 1 November 2026, eight days and five weeks after this record was written.

Three dates on the autonomous-university route are derived rather than published and are marked provisional: NTU's actual-results deadline of 9 July 2027 is 6 July plus three days; the IBO transcript authorisation of 30 June 2027 is the last day satisfying NTU's "before July 2027"; and NUS's outcome date of 21 July 2027 is a reading of "the third week of July". Each carries a note saying so.

portal.name: No shared application — six autonomous universities, six forms, six fees, six deadlines. There is a shared acceptance: every offer you hold across them is settled once, in the Joint Acceptance Portal.

deadlines.label: LASALLE College of the Arts — main application window for the August 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: The earliest deadline on this page by a wide margin, and easy to miss. LASALLE opens on 1 October 2026 and asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, with outcomes announced by 23 December 2026 — eight months before IB results. LASALLE adds two hedges of its own: "the timeline provided serves as a general guide. Actual outcome release dates may vary", and that future application windows may open if programme seats remain available. So this is a window rather than the only chance, but it is the one that gets first pick of the seats, and the outcome dates are softer than the application ones. Music runs on its own later date and has its own entry below.

deadlines.notes: NTU does not publish a calendar date. It says actual IB results must be submitted within three days of the results release in July 2027, and the IB releases on 6 July 2027, so 9 July 2027 is arithmetic on those two facts rather than a date NTU has printed. steps: Work out which of the three Singapores you are applying to. The six Autonomous Universities, the two arts institutions under the University of the Arts Singapore, and the private institutions and foreign branch campuses run on different calendars, different rules and different money.
If the arts are in play, act first. LASALLE opens on 1 October 2026, two weeks before NTU, and asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, six weeks before NUS opens.

Decide about the MOE Tuition Grant with your family before you fill in any application form, because you elect it on the form itself. Taking it cuts tuition by roughly a third to almost half and commits you to three years of full-time work for a Singapore entity after graduation, guaranteed by two sureties who are jointly liable if you do not serve it.

Apply to each autonomous university separately, with predicted grades, transcript, personal statement and references, and a separate fee each time. NUS closes 17 February 2027; NTU closes 19 March 2027.
Check the programme is open to a May-session IB candidate. NTU excludes Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, and Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education) outright.
Authorise the IB organisation to send your transcript directly to the university. NTU requires this before July 2027 and will not release an outcome without it.
Expect an interview, portfolio or written test for the selective routes — SUTD and SIT interview as a matter of course, and NUS Law, medicine and the scholars’ programmes all add assessment.
Keep the first fortnight of July 2027 clear. NTU wants your actual results within three days of release.
Accept one offer through the Joint Acceptance Portal. The windows for 2027 are not yet announced.

Apply for a Student’s Pass through ICA’s SOLAR system once the university sponsors you, then register and sign the Tuition Grant Agreement in Singapore in the autumn — it needs a Singpass, which needs the Student’s Pass first.
Apply for campus accommodation the day your offer arrives. It is allocated separately and is the only realistic first-year option.
application.selectionNotes: Academic, with assessment layered on. NUS and NTU are large and selective and decide largely on grades; SMU is specialised in business, law, economics, social science and computing; SUTD assesses holistically on academics, traits and a portfolio with an interview for selected candidates, and says its approach is significantly different from most universities; SIT interviews every shortlisted applicant. LASALLE and NAFA decide on portfolio and audition, and their deadlines fall months before everyone else’s.

tuitionEuEea.value: Singapore does not differentiate by EU status — the categories are Singapore Citizen, Singapore Permanent Resident and International Student. As a European applicant you are an International Student.

tuitionNonEu.value: NTU, for students accepted in 2026, with the tuition fee fixed at the 2026 rate for the whole degree: International Student with the MOE Tuition Grant roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 per year; International Student without the grant SGD 36,350 (non-lab) to SGD 40,600 (lab-based) per year, inclusive of 9% GST. Medicine, non-subsidised only, SGD 91,250 per year for non-ASEAN internationals. Renaissance Engineering, non-subsidised only, SGD 32,000. NUS, for students admitted in AY2026/2027 (fixed for the cohort): international students with the Tuition Grant SGD 21,400 a year in computing, engineering and humanities and sciences, SGD 22,200 in business, SGD 30,450 in law; without the grant SGD 33,400–39,700 (SGD 44,450 law), inclusive of GST. AY2027/2028 fees are published in February to April 2027. SMU and SUTD figures are not given here.
tuitionNonEu.year: AY2026/27 entrants, fixed for the degree duration (NTU and NUS)

costs.applicationFee: Per university: NTU SGD 25 for international applicants. Check the others with each university.
notes: The NTU table distinguishes lab-based from non-lab programmes and ASEAN from other international students. Read it directly rather than relying on a single headline figure — and note that the published table's lab/non-lab labelling is worth double-checking against the PDF.
The key number is the difference between the two columns: roughly SGD 15,000–19,000 a year, or SGD 60,000–75,000 over a four-year degree. That is what the three-year service obligation is worth.
Non-subsidised fees include 9% GST; subsidised fees are quoted exclusive of it.
NTU states that the annual tuition fee is fixed at the year-of-entry rate for the duration of the degree, which removes the risk of mid-degree increases.
No official living-cost figure is quoted here. Campus accommodation is considerably cheaper than the private rental market, which is expensive.

funding: MOE Tuition Grant — the main subsidy and the main commitment. International students elect it on the admission application form, confirm it when accepting the offer, and then sign a Tuition Grant Agreement with two sureties that contractually obliges them to work in a Singapore entity for three years after graduation. At NTU it takes the fee from roughly SGD 36,350–40,600 a year to roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 — about SGD 60,000–75,000 across a four-year degree. It runs for the normal programme duration only, so a repeated year is unsubsidised.

Declining the grant is a real option, not a failure. You pay the full unsubsidised fee, you carry no obligation and you need no sureties. That is the right choice if you intend to return to Europe after graduating, and it should be a decision rather than a default.

Breaking the bond, or withdrawing from the course, makes you and both sureties liable for liquidated damages — on the outstanding bond period if you break it, and on the whole grant received plus 10% compounded interest a year if you withdraw mid-course.

Merit scholarships: NUS, NTU and SMU all run competitive scholarships for outstanding international entrants, typically covering tuition plus a living allowance. Most carry their own bond conditions — sometimes six years rather than three. Check each one’s terms before applying.

ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarships and similar regional awards are for nationals of ASEAN countries, so they are not open to EU/EEA citizens; if you hold another nationality, check the eligibility list.
Whether the Tuition Grant reaches LASALLE, NAFA or the private institutions for an international student is not established here.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: Part-time work is restricted on a Student’s Pass — see 'Living there' below. Do not plan to fund yourself by working.
workRights: Full-time students on a Student's Pass at the institutions MOM lists (NUS and NTU among them) may work up to 16 hours a week in term without a work pass, and without a limit during vacations. Once the Student's Pass expires, a work pass is needed. Work is not a realistic way to close a funding gap in Singapore.
residency: EU citizenship gives no advantage. Once you accept an offer, the university sponsors your Student's Pass application through ICA's SOLAR system, which must be completed before you travel. On arrival you complete formalities at ICA and receive the pass. Many European citizens, Danes included, do not need a visa to enter Singapore as a visitor (check ICA's list for your nationality), but you cannot study on a visitor pass.
housing: Campus accommodation — halls of residence at NUS and NTU, the residential colleges, and SUTD's housing — is the only sensible first-year option and is allocated separately from the admission. It is not guaranteed for all four years at every university, and some allocate by a points system based on participation in campus activities. The private market in Singapore is expensive and usually means a room in a shared HDB flat. Apply for housing the day your offer arrives.
healthcare: International students are normally required to be covered by the university's own medical insurance scheme, charged as a compulsory fee alongside tuition. Singapore's healthcare is not free at the point of use, and your EHIC does not apply. Check what the university scheme actually covers — it is usually hospitalisation rather than routine care.

The grant covers only the normal duration of the programme.

submissionItems.label: Two sureties for the Tuition Grant Agreement
submissionItems.destinationOfItem: MOE's TG&S Portal, signed digitally — sureties do not need to be in Singapore.
submissionItems.note: Two people of any nationality, over 21 and under 65, not undischarged bankrupts, not themselves bonded, and with the financial means to cover the liability. MOE encourages immediate family. They are jointly liable with you for liquidated damages, so they need to read the agreement as carefully as you do.

sources.title: A Tuition Grant Agreement requires two sureties of any nationality, aged over 21 and under 65, who are not undischarged bankrupts, are not themselves Tuition Grant or Service Obligation applicants or recipients with an outstanding obligation, and are not surety to another recipient who failed to fulfil theirs.

Breaking a Tuition Grant bond makes the student and both sureties liable for liquidated damages on the outstanding bond period; withdrawing from the course makes them liable for the grant received plus 10% compounded interest a year. Only full-time employment after graduation counts towards the bond, deferment for postgraduate study must be approved at least eight weeks in advance, and obtaining Singapore citizenship releases the student from the three-year obligation.

submissionItems.label: Authorisation for the university to receive your transcript from the IB organisation
submissionItems.destinationOfItem: The International Baccalaureate Organization, not the university.
submissionItems.note: NTU makes this mandatory before July 2027 and will not release an outcome without it. NUS also makes it mandatory for every IB applicant: tell your IB coordinator to release your transcript to the National University of Singapore, institute code 000690.

sources.title: For IB Diploma holders entering in AY2027-28, NTU's online application runs 15 October 2026 to 19 March 2027, supporting documents are due 22 March 2027, offers are released between March and May 2027, and a student sitting the May 2027 session must submit actual IB results within three days of their release in July 2027 — but may not apply at all to Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, or Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education).

NUS admits IB Diploma holders of any nationality, requires English to be one of the IB subjects, and requires every applicant to authorise the IB to release their transcript to NUS (institute code 000690).

supplementarySteps: Apply to each university separately. Six universities, six forms, six fees, six deadlines — NUS closes on 17 February 2027 and NTU on 19 March 2027, and the two are not interchangeable.

If you are sitting the May 2027 session, check the programme is open to you at all. NTU excludes May-session IB candidates from Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, and Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education) outright.
Decide about the Tuition Grant before you apply, because you elect it on the application form.
Keep the first fortnight of July 2027 clear. NTU wants your actual results within three days of release.
Apply for campus accommodation the day an offer arrives. It is allocated separately from admission and is the only realistic first-year option.

sources.title: For IB Diploma holders entering in AY2027-28, NTU's online application runs 15 October 2026 to 19 March 2027, supporting documents are due 22 March 2027, offers are released between March and May 2027, and a student sitting the May 2027 session must submit actual IB results within three days of their release in July 2027 — but may not apply at all to Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, or Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education).

For AY2027/2028 NUS runs the IB Diploma as its own applicant group with an application period of 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027, the same window as for other international qualifications, and tells IB applicants sitting the May 2027 examination that they will hear by the third week of July 2027. Offers are accepted through a shared Joint Acceptance Portal whose windows are not yet confirmed.

International students obtain the MOE Tuition Grant by electing it on the online admission application form, then decide whether to accept their place with or without it, then register and sign the Tuition Grant Agreement with two sureties after term has started — and by signing are contractually obliged to work in a Singapore entity for three years upon graduation. The grant covers only the normal duration of the programme.
Offers from Singapore's autonomous universities are accepted through a single shared Joint Acceptance Portal by a joint acceptance deadline, rather than to each university separately.

SUTD publishes a 2026 admissions application window of 2 January to 2 March 2026 for all qualifications other than the Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level, which runs from the day of A-Level results release to 19 March 2026. No 2027 window is published. SUTD assesses holistically on academics, traits and portfolio, with an interview for selected candidates.

SIT's 2026 cycle ran online applications from 8 January to 19 March 2026, with interviews from mid-February to mid-May, outcomes mid-April to mid-May, acceptance on 25 May 2026 through the Joint Acceptance Portal and an appeal window of 26 May to 2 June 2026. Every shortlisted applicant is interviewed. No 2027 dates are published.

NUS admits IB Diploma holders of any nationality, requires English to be one of the IB subjects, and requires every applicant to authorise the IB to release their transcript to NUS (institute code 000690).

notes: The applicant group is non-eu rather than any because Singapore's categories are Singapore Citizen, Singapore Permanent Resident and International Student, and almost everything on this route that differs — the fee, the Tuition Grant election, the sureties, the bond, the Student's Pass — differs because the student is in the third category. A route written for "any" would describe a Singaporean's experience and mislead ours.

Dates are established for NUS and NTU only. SUTD, SIT and SMU publish their 2026 cycle and not their 2027 one (SMU read in a browser on 2026-09-24). SUSS says applications for its July 2027 intake open in November 2026, with no dates yet.

The three provisional dates on this route are all derived rather than published: NTU's actual-results deadline is 6 July plus three days, the IBO transcript authorisation is the last day that satisfies "before July 2027", and the NUS outcome date is a reading of "the third week of July". Each says so in its own note.

routes.label: Applying to a Singapore private institution or foreign branch campus, 2027

milestones.label: IB results released
milestones.note: These institutions mostly run trimesters with several intakes a year rather than one August start, so results landing in July are less of a cliff here than at an autonomous university. That is a statement about the structure and not about any deadline, because none is published.

sources.title: The IB is taken to release May 2027 results to candidates on 6 July 2027. This is an inference from the three preceding sessions and is NOT established by the source cited, which could not be opened.

submissionItems.label: Check the institution's Private Education Institution registration and its expiry
submissionItems.destinationOfItem: The institution's own page, where the registration number and period are published.
submissionItems.note: Singapore registers private education institutions for a fixed term rather than chartering them indefinitely, and the expiry date is public — Curtin Singapore's runs 20 May 2026 to 19 May 2032. A registration expiring inside the length of your degree is a question to ask before enrolling.

sources.title: Curtin Singapore operates as a registered Private Education Institution — registration number 200804822R, valid 20 May 2026 to 19 May 2032 — under the Australian CRICOS provider code 00301J, and publishes no undergraduate application deadline.

supplementarySteps: Establish who awards the degree before anything else. Curtin Singapore and James Cook University Singapore award Australian degrees, DigiPen Singapore an American one, ESSEC Asia-Pacific a French one, and SIM Global Education delivers several partner universities' degrees without awarding any of its own.

Assume the MOE Tuition Grant does not apply. It is a subsidy to Singapore's own institutions, and none of these is an Autonomous University — which also means no service obligation, no sureties and no bond.
Ask each institution directly for its deadlines. None of them publishes one for 2027 on the pages consulted here.
For ESSEC's Global BBA, the application is made to ESSEC in France on the French cycle, not to the Singapore campus.

sources.title: Curtin Singapore operates as a registered Private Education Institution — registration number 200804822R, valid 20 May 2026 to 19 May 2032 — under the Australian CRICOS provider code 00301J, and publishes no undergraduate application deadline.

notes: Five institutions, no dates. This is the least-researched route in this Destination and the record says so rather than implying these institutions admit continuously. James Cook University Singapore's pages refused automated retrieval; Curtin, DigiPen, SIM and ESSEC publish no undergraduate application deadline on the pages consulted.

Not established: whether the MOE Tuition Grant reaches any of these institutions. The assumption recorded above — that it does not, because they are not Autonomous Universities — is stated as an assumption in the step rather than as a finding, and should be confirmed with the institution.
"Apply directly" here is a researched finding rather than a placeholder: none of these institutions sits in a shared admissions system, and each runs its own form on its own calendar.

systems.name: Joint Acceptance Portal

jurisdiction.authority: Singapore's six Autonomous Universities, acting together
jurisdiction.area: NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS

coverage.includes: Accepting an undergraduate offer from any of the six Autonomous Universities — NUS, NTU, SIT, SMU, SUSS and SUTD. Every offer a student holds across them appears in one portal and is settled in one exercise.
coverage.excludes: Applying. There is no shared application: each university runs its own form, its own fee and its own deadline, and those deadlines are months apart. Also excluded are LASALLE and NAFA, the private education institutions and the foreign branch campuses, none of which is an Autonomous University.

choiceRules.note: A student may hold offers from several Autonomous Universities at once and chooses between them in the Joint Acceptance Exercise rather than replying to each separately. Applicants may log in during the exercise to modify their selection.

systems.identityRequirement: An applicant account at each university, and — separately, and only once you are in Singapore with a Student's Pass — a Singpass, which is what the MOE Tuition Grant registration runs on.
systems.decisionModel: Decisions are made independently by each university on its own criteria and released on its own calendar, generally between March and July. The portal does not rank, match or allocate; it is the acceptance step only.
systems.replyModel: Acceptance is indicated once, in the Joint Acceptance Portal, by a joint acceptance deadline shared across the Autonomous Universities. NUS states that an acceptance indicated through the portal is reflected on its own applicant portal three calendar days after the acceptance deadline.

sources.title: Offers from Singapore's autonomous universities are accepted through a single shared Joint Acceptance Portal by a joint acceptance deadline, rather than to each university separately.

For AY2027/2028 NUS runs the IB Diploma as its own applicant group with an application period of 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027, the same window as for other international qualifications, and tells IB applicants sitting the May 2027 examination that they will hear by the third week of July 2027. Offers are accepted through a shared Joint Acceptance Portal whose windows are not yet confirmed.

notes: Singapore is usually described as having no central admissions system. For applying that is true. For accepting it is not, and the difference is worth a student's attention: the choice between Singapore universities is made once, against one deadline, rather than offer by offer.
The joint acceptance windows for AY2027/2028 are published by NUS as "To be Confirmed". SIT's 2026 equivalent fell on 25 May 2026. Neither is recorded as a 2027 date.

Not established: whether an international student uses the same portal and the same deadline as a Singaporean one, and what happens to a Tuition Grant election at this point. Both pages consulted describe the portal without distinguishing applicant groups.

additionalGuidance.title: More about studying here
additionalGuidance.text: Singapore runs entirely in English and reads the IB directly. The headline price is not the price: the MOE Tuition Grant cuts international tuition by roughly a third to almost half, and in exchange you sign a contract, guaranteed by two sureties, to work for a Singapore entity for three years after graduating — chosen by ticking a box on the application form. There are three Singapores: six Autonomous Universities sharing an August intake and one acceptance portal, two arts colleges whose deadline falls the previous November, and private campuses awarding a foreign degree.
